title: GAIA GitHub label registry
description: Constrains .gaia/labels.json: the single machine-readable source of truth for every GitHub label GAIA creates, syncs, and documents. A malformed edit fails this cheap validation before any consumer runs. Cross-entry constraints (unique names, unique colors, no em dashes or en dashes in a description) are not expressible in JSON Schema and live in the validation layer the gaia labels commands run, and its tests, instead.

name.description: The literal GitHub label name. Unique across the registry.

color.description: 6 lowercase hex digits, no '#'. Unique across every entry whose color is non-null. null for a blocked entry (nothing renders it).

description.description: At most 100 characters (GitHub's limit). No em dash or en dash; enforced in the Zod layer, not here.

audience.description: Maintainer entries are stripped from the shipped bundle and never synced to an adopter repo.

features.description: The label is created when any listed feature is enabled. An empty list means always create.

managed.description: false means document only: sync reconciles the description but never creates, recolors, or deletes.

deprecated.description: Kept in the registry and on the page for history, never created on a fresh repo.

blocked.description: The label must not exist. Never created; reported when found; deleted only on the maintainer repo under --enforce-blocked and only when zero issues carry it.

renamedFrom.description: Previous names, in order. Sync uses `gh label edit <old> --name <new>` when an old name exists on the repo and the new one does not.

reason.description: A non-empty string on every blocked entry, null on every other entry.
